item.text: The batch executor is in `src/exec/mod.rs`; the current shape appears to build one command containing every result, which explains the OS `E2BIG` failure. I’m reading that implementation plus the command runner now, then I’ll make the smallest local change.

I’ve got the failure point: `generate_and_execute_batch` collects all paths and appends them to a single `Command`. I’m checking the nearby exec-batch tests so the fix fits the existing behavior, especially sorting and placeholder handling.

11	/// An event loop that listens for inputs from the `rx` receiver. Each received input will
12	/// generate a command with the supplied command template. The generated command will then
13	/// be executed, and this process will continue until the receiver's sender has closed.
14	pub fn job(
15	    rx: Arc<Mutex<Receiver<WorkerResult>>>,
16	    cmd: Arc<CommandTemplate>,
17	    out_perm: Arc<Mutex<()>>,
18	    show_filesystem_errors: bool,
19	    buffer_output: bool,
20	) -> ExitCode {
21	    let mut results: Vec<ExitCode> = Vec::new();
22	    loop {
23	        // Create a lock on the shared receiver for this thread.
24	        let lock = rx.lock().unwrap();
25	
26	        // Obtain the next result from the receiver, else if the channel
27	        // has closed, exit from the loop
28	        let value: PathBuf = match lock.recv() {
29	            Ok(WorkerResult::Entry(val)) => val,
30	            Ok(WorkerResult::Error(err)) => {
31	                if show_filesystem_errors {
32	                    print_error(err.to_string());
33	                }
34	                continue;
35	            }
36	            Err(_) => break,
37	        };
38	
39	        // Drop the lock so that other threads can read from the receiver.
40	        drop(lock);
41	        // Generate a command, execute it and store its exit code.
42	        results.push(cmd.generate_and_execute(&value, Arc::clone(&out_perm), buffer_output))
43	    }
44	    // Returns error in case of any error.
45	    merge_exitcodes(results)
46	}

item.text: The repository already has `libc` on Unix, so I can use `sysconf(_SC_ARG_MAX)` without adding dependencies. The robust bit is accounting for environment size and fixed command arguments, then flushing chunks before the OS rejects the spawn.

I’m going to preserve the existing `cmd prefix <all paths> suffix` argument order for the one allowed placeholder, just split the path list into as many invocations as fit. The sizing will be conservative because environment variables and pointer overhead count too on Unix.
